Hi Priya / Tom  thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align internal stakeholders and get procurement moving.

Call recap (high level):
- Use case: real-time credit decisioning + conversational customer support for high-value retail flows.
- Expected peak throughput: ~500 concurrent requests (approx 300300 QPS with batching).
- Quality targets: parity with current in-house model on NLU intents + fewer false-positives on risk signals.

Open decision criteria we discussed (please confirm):
1) Latency: you mentioned strict 99th percentile targets  can you confirm p99 target for generation?
2) Deployment mode: are you leaning to Dedicated (reserved GPUs) vs. Private (VPC / on-prem) for initial rollout?
3) SLA: required uptime / response-time SLOs and acceptance criteria for breach/remedy.
4) Procurement steps & timing: who is the economic buyer and what timeline does procurement/legal estimate?

Action items from Redwood side:
- I can put together a short proposal/SOW and a performance appendix with p50/p95/p99 numbers by deployment mode.
- Rishi will scope security/compliance artifacts you requested.

Attachments: Redwood_Product_Sheet_v3.pdf (high-level perf profiles + deployment options).

Would you be able to confirm the four decision points above by EOD Wednesday so we can get a draft SOW to you next week?

Hi Marissa  thanks for the summary. I pulled answers together after checking with Tom and Legal. See inline below and attached a security questionnaire and our procurement checklist.

> 1) Latency: you mentioned strict 99th percentile targets  can you confirm p99 target for generation?
We are targeting p99 <= 250ms for single-turn text generation for our credit decision endpoint (short prompts, ~60120 tokens). For longer multi-step agent flows we can accept p99 <= 450ms. P50/P95 targets are less strict but useful for sizing.

> 2) Deployment mode: Dedicated vs Private
We prefer Dedicated initially (reserved capacity in us-west) to ensure predictable throughput and cost; Private (VPC) is acceptable for the later security review if needed, but procurement prefers Dedicated for faster onboarding.

> 3) SLA: required uptime / SLOs
Baseline ask: 99.9% uptime for production endpoints, with a remediation SLA (credit + escalation path). For performance, an SLO tied to p99 latency breaches would be ideal  we'll want to see your proposed measurement approach.

> 4) Procurement steps & timing / economic buyer
Economic buyer: Tom Edwards (tom.edwards@finova.com)  head of Payments.
Procurement/legal: Elena Morales (cc'd) will own contract redlines; procurement checklist attached outlines our standard approval timeline (~336 weeks once we have final SOW + pricing).

Attachments: Finova_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx, Finova_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

Next steps: if you can send a draft SOW with a perf appendix (p50/p95/p99 across Dedicated vs. Private) and a preliminary pricing estimate (example: committed monthly spend for guaranteed capacity), we'll circulate internally.

Thanks  Priya
